focus: Practical software engineering, scientific research tools, and automation across sectors
title: A Green Test Run Is a Starting Point, Not a Guarantee
utility_use_case: A research group can scan a staged microscopy export directory before archiving it. The report provides exact-content groups and a potential redundant-byte estimate, helping the team prioritize review. Researchers still decide whether copies serve distinct provenance or workflow needs; the utility only reports and never removes files.

editorial_review.summary: Qualified claims that matching SHA-256 digests establish byte identity. The utility groups files by size and digest, which is strong practical evidence but not a mathematical proof of identical bytes.

edits.old: A report of matching hashes establishes byte identity for the files examined, not that the files are operationally interchangeable.
edits.new: Matching file sizes and hashes are strong evidence that the files have identical bytes, not proof or a sign that they are operationally interchangeable.

edits.old: Files are grouped as duplicates only when both size and digest match.
edits.new: Files are reported as duplicates only when both size and digest match. As with any hash-based comparison, this is strong practical evidence, not a mathematical proof of byte identity.

glossary_edits.definition: A cryptographic hash function that maps file bytes to a fixed-length digest. The duplicate-report utility groups files when their sizes and SHA-256 digests match. This is strong practical evidence of identical bytes, not a mathematical proof or evidence that files are interchangeable in a workflow.
